players.product: 8-inch and 12-inch wafer foundry and technology services (fabs in Shanghai, Beijing, Tianjin, Shenzhen)

quarterly_data.signal: FY2025 results (annual report): revenue US$9,326.8 million, up 16.2% year-on-year, primarily on higher wafer shipments; wafer revenue US$8,796.4 million, up 17.5%; gross margin 21.0%, up 3.0 percentage points on higher shipments, higher utilisation and product mix despite a substantial increase in depreciation; profit attributable to owners of the company US$685.1 million, up 39.0%; EBITDA margin 56.4% (54.5% in 2024); R&D expenses US$773.6 million (8.3% of revenue); government funding recognised in other operating income US$472,721 thousand.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2025 revenue US$9,326.8 million (+16.2%); gross margin 21.0%; profit attributable US$685.1 million (+39.0%)

quarterly_data.signal: 2025 operations (annual report): wafer shipments rose 20.9% to 9,697 thousand standard logic 8-inch-equivalent wafers; average selling price (wafer revenue divided by shipments) US$907 per wafer versus US$933 in 2024; utilisation 93.5%, up 8 percentage points (chairman's letter); monthly capacity reached 1,058,750 standard logic 8-inch-equivalent wafers by end-2025 (the chairman: monthly capacity scale exceeded 1 million); 2025 production 10,126,337 wafers, and wafer inventory rose 36.8% to 1,596,016 pieces, primarily due to the pre-build of inventory.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 shipments 9,697 thousand 8-inch-eq wafers (+20.9%); ASP US$907 per wafer; utilisation 93.5%; capacity 1,058,750 wafers/month at end-2025

quarterly_data.signal: 2025 revenue mix (annual report): by region China 85.6%, America 11.6%, Eurasia 2.8% (2024: 84.6%, 12.4%, 3.0%); wafer revenue by application smartphone 23.1%, computer and tablet 14.8%, consumer electronics 43.2%, connectivity and IoT 7.9%, industrial and automotive 11.0% (2024: smartphone 27.8%, industrial and automotive 7.8%); 12-inch wafers 77.1% and 8-inch wafers 22.9% of wafer revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025: China 85.6% of revenue; consumer electronics 43.2% and industrial and automotive 11.0% of wafer revenue

quarterly_data.signal: Customer and supplier concentration (annual report): sales to the largest customer and to the five largest customers were 8.0% and 35.8% of 2025 revenue, with no related-party sales among the five, and no single customer reached 10% of revenue; purchases from the five largest raw-materials suppliers were 25.7% of 2025 raw-materials purchases. At year-end the largest customer and the five largest customers accounted for 16.9% and 53.2% of trade receivables (2024: 20.3% and 50.4%). The company describes its major customers as IC design companies and IDM companies at home and abroad.
quarterly_data.figure: largest customer 8.0% and five largest 35.8% of 2025 revenue; five largest raw-materials suppliers 25.7% of purchases

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 guidance (annual report, assuming no significant change in the external environment): revenue growth expected to be higher than the industry average in the same markets, and capital expenditure expected to be roughly flat compared with 2025. The company also says it expects to maintain significant capital expenditure in 2026, expected to exceed 20% of its latest audited net assets, and keeps undistributed profits for capacity expansion (no cash dividend proposed). Outlook in the business plan: reshoring of the industrial chain from overseas and domestic customers' new products replacing legacy overseas products will persist; robust AI-driven memory demand has squeezed memory supply for other sectors such as mobile phones, particularly the mid-to-low-end market, leaving end-product makers with tight supply and rising memory prices that may reduce end demand; the company says its technology reserves in BCD, analog, memory, MCU and mid-to-high-end display driver leave it well positioned to drive continued revenue growth in 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 capex roughly flat vs 2025; 2026 capex expected to exceed 20% of latest audited net assets

quarterly_data.signal: 2025 cash flow and balance sheet (annual report): payments for property, plant and equipment, intangible assets and land-use rights totalled US$8,403.5 million, up 9.6%, most of the capital expenditure used for capacity expansion; net cash from operating activities US$3,194.3 million (+0.6%); depreciation and amortisation US$3,810,010 thousand (US$3,223,063 thousand in 2024); cash and cash equivalents US$5,872,500 thousand at year-end; contract liabilities (customer prepayments for wafers not yet transferred) fell 49.5% to US$599.4 million from US$1,185.9 million on lower advance receipts, while trade and other receivables rose 70.5%, mainly from adjusted credit terms for some customers and higher value-added tax to be deducted.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 capex payments US$8,403.5 million (+9.6%); contract liabilities US$599.4 million (US$1,185.9 million in 2024)

quarterly_data.signal: 2025 R&D platform progress (annual report): 28nm ULL platform - new-generation PDK, standard cell libraries and memory compilers released and being validated in multiple types of products; 28nm SST e-Flash platform for high-end MCU (vehicle domain controller, ADAS) - critical process development completed; 65nm RF-SOI - new-generation PDK released and being introduced into new products; 90nm BCD - new low- and medium-voltage PDKs released and in customers' new product designs; 8-inch BCD and analog - product engagement for the next-generation automotive BCD platform completed, next-generation medium/high-voltage BCD PDK released, SOI BCD process and device development completed; 0.18 micron eNVM for automotive electronics - process development completed, PDK under development; display drivers - next-generation medium-size platform in mass production, large-size process development completed. The company also established an advanced packaging research institute. Patents: 14,511 granted (12,621 invention patents) at the end of 2025.

Equity transactions (annual report): on September 8, 2025 SMIC agreed to acquire the 49% equity interest in its subsidiary SMNC held by China IC Fund, Beijing Semiconductor Manufacturing and Equipment Equity Investment Center, Beijing E-Town International Investment and Development, Zhongguancun Development Group and Beijing Industrial Development Investment Management, to be paid by issuing RMB (A) shares; the final terms were set in a December 29, 2025 supplemental agreement, an extraordinary general meeting approved the deal on February 12, 2026 and the SSE accepted the application on February 25, 2026. Separately, a planned sale of SMIC Holdings' 14.832% stake in associate Ningbo Semiconductor International (NSI) to Hunan Goke Microelectronics, signed June 5, 2025, was terminated on November 28, 2025, and SMIC Holdings retains the 14.832% stake.
quarterly_data.figure: 49% of SMNC to be acquired; 14.832% NSI stake retained

quarterly_data.signal: Legal proceedings (annual report): in a Hong Kong International Arbitration Centre case that PDF Solutions brought against SMIC subsidiary SMIC New Technology Research and Development (Shanghai) (arbitration notice received May 7, 2020), the tribunal rendered an award on November 12, 2025 under which SMIC New Technology is to pay the relevant fees to PDF Solutions; SMIC New Technology contends the award is manifestly improper, with material procedural irregularities and substantive errors in applying pivotal legal principles, and has applied to the High Court of the Hong Kong SAR to set it aside. 2025 other losses included US$73,410 thousand of 'others', which the company says mainly included recognised related expenses for an arbitration award.
quarterly_data.figure: US$73,410 thousand 'others' in 2025 other losses, mainly arbitration-award related expenses

quarterly_data.signal: Export-control designations (annual report risk factors): SMIC was added to the U.S. Entity List in 2020 and some of its affiliated companies were added to the Entity List 'Footnote 5' in 2024, which the company says brings challenges to its supply-chain security and business stability; further tightening of export controls or license reviews could tighten supply of restricted equipment, raw materials, parts, software and service support and restrict business cooperation; some investors may be barred from buying or selling its securities under the U.S. Treasury's Non-SDN Chinese Military-Industrial Complex Entities List (NS-CMIC List).
